title: An evidential operator separates asserted procedures from conditional procedures
summary: A recurring form could encode evidential commitment: it marks a procedure as asserted in the source record, while its absence leaves the procedure conditional or merely proposed.

design.unit: complete procedure record with an explicit asserted/conditional status contrast
design.contrast: commitment marker versus ordinary lexical content
design.prediction: If the marker is evidential, independently coded asserted records should contain it at a higher fixed rate than conditional/proposed records, after matching procedure type.
design.countermodel: The proposed rule may be an analyst projection: the same observations could arise from a context-conditioned lexical or editorial convention without the proposed semantic operator.
design.falsifier: A held set of status-matched records shows the marker tracks material type or position but not commitment; the evidential account then loses its restricted prediction.
design.principal_risk: The status labels require independent historical annotation; current availability is unknown. This is near modality/prohibition proposals but targets assertion status, not permission or forbiddenness.
